text.p: Late trading on the LME on Tuesday was volatile, with copper and aluminium witnessing savage late movements prior to a mostly lower close for the complex.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.66 points to 243.09.

Zinc highlighted the day's trend, falling steeply after a 1,400-tonne stock increase that gave credence to talk of Chinese shipments of some 20,000 tonnes of metal to Singapore. Prices were pulled under $1,500, and now look set for further chart-based losses. Last business was at $1,480 a tonne, down $63 from Monday's kerb.

Copper appeared to be set to conclusively break out of the $2,260/70 to $2,320/30 band, but failed to trigger the expected sell-stops in the mid-$2,250s. This averted the possibility of a sell-off to $2,220/30, and induced a late covering rally. Three months ended at $2,278, up $4.
Aluminium cascaded below $1,700 briefly, but was buttressed by chart-based support, and with copper rallying managed to close at $1,715.
Nickel fell to fresh intra-day lows during the kerb, but remained volatile with the market seen as oversold in the short-term.
Lead dropped to a fresh 22-month low of $596 today, but the pace of trading was slower than in the other metals and the decline was somewhat muted. Three months finished at $598, down $8.
Tin was battered by a combination of trade and Chinese selling as well as liquidation sales, and dropped under $5,400 briefly before concluding at $5,415, down $95 from Monday.
Alloy was indicated at a softer $1,515/25 at the close.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower on moderate volumes Tuesday, after the U.S dollar and stocks and bonds recovered further ground early in the session. COMEX December gold ended down $1.70 an ounce at $330.80, retreating from a two week high at $333.40 Monday to a session low at $328.70, before some recovery occurred near the close. In the bullion market, spot gold retreated to a session low around $324.80, from two week highs around $329.20 Monday.

IPE Brent was boosted on Tuesday by renewed strength in the U.S. gasoline market and broke through the $18.80 resistance level in a late surge to close 26 cents up at $18.84 a barrel, brokers said. The September contract gained 10-15 cents after the NYMEX market opened but was then trapped in the $18.72-$18.79 range for much of the afternoon, bouncing off the $18.80 ceiiing and consolidating.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower in a bearish reaction to USDA's hike in its 1997 U.S. wheat production forecast and on an increase by the government in its forecast for 1997-98 production and ending stocks of foreign wheat, traders said. Wheat closed three cents per bushel lower to 1/4 higher, with September down 2-3/4 at $3.61 a bushel.
